result.reason: The passage introduces the dispute with 'itmar' and presents the core question of one who performs avodah zarah me'ahavah umiyirah, which is exactly what heading 0 ('Acts Without Belief') describes in its prose, whereas heading 2 ('Abaye vs. Rava') only contains the conclusion of the dispute without introducing the case itself.
All four items constitute Abaye's proof from the mishnah and Rava's rebuttal via Rabbi Yirmiya's explanation — exactly what the 'Abaye's Proof' prose section describes.
The passage is Abaye's baraita proof involving the Haman bowing case, which is exactly what the 'Haman & Bowing' section's prose describes in detail.
The passage directly presents Rava's 'keHaman velo keHaman' distinction, which is precisely what the prose under 'Rava's Distinction' explains and analyzes.

All three items together form Abaye's proof from the baraita about the kohen mashiach in avodah zarah — the baraita text (item 1), the points of agreement (item 2), and the Gemara's analysis of what 'shiggas ma'aseh' means in this context (item 3) — which matches exactly what heading 4 ('Braita Introduced') describes, and the current placement is correct.

The passage describes the second scenario (seeing a statue and bowing) and specifically the sub-case where 'he accepted it as a deity — meizid hu,' which is exactly what the 'Three Scenarios' prose section describes when it says 'if he accepted it as a deity — meizid hu — he is fully liable.'

All four items form the continuous Rava-centered exchange: item 1 sets up the me'ahava umiyirah conclusion that Rava must reject, items 2-4 give Rava's response (be'omer mutar), the challenge (that is he'elam davar), and the resolution (omer mutar legamrei vs. kiyum miktzas), which is precisely what candidate 3 'Rava's Case' prose describes.
The passage is the baraita taught by Rabbi Zakkai before Rabbi Yochanan, which is exactly what heading 0 'Zakkai Teaching' describes in its prose.
The passage is Rabbi Yochanan's terse rejection ('go teach it outside'), which is exactly what the 'Yochanan Rejects' section's prose describes.

All three items present the Rabbi Yosei/Rabbi Natan dispute about kindling fire on Shabbat and its application to hishtachavah — exactly the content described in the 'Fire Debate' prose, which explicitly summarizes this baraita and Rabbi Abba's conclusion about bowing.

All three items comprise Rav Yosef's objection and its supporting baraita — exactly the content described in the 'Yosef Clarifies' prose, which explicitly paraphrases Rav Yosef's argument about Rabbi Yosi deriving chiluk melachos from me'achas mehena rather than from fire.

The passage is Rabbi Yonatan's derivation from the verse 'me'achas mehena' explaining Rabbi Yosei's reasoning through the four terms (achat, me'achat, heina, meheinah) and the two compound cases, which is precisely what the 'Pasuk Explained' prose describes.
The passage specifically discusses the Shimon/shin-mem example to illustrate 'achat' and 'me'achat', which is exactly what the 'Shimon Case' prose describes.

All 10 items deal with applying the 'achas mehena/heina/meheinah' framework to avodah zarah — including the four primary avodos, subcategories, the compound cases of zadon/shogeg, the difficulty of defining shgegat avodah zarah, the mei'ahavah umiyirah answer, and Rava's 'omer mutar' resolution — which is precisely what the 'Avodah Framework' prose describes.

Item 1 raises the challenge that the verses in question appear in a context of differentiated korbanot (par/seir/kisbah), which perfectly matches candidate 0's prose about the gemara withdrawing the suggestion because me'achas mehena presupposes this structure — while item 2 (the baraita about v'shavin she'bis'eirah k'yachid) completes the same argument by showing avodah zarah has no such differentiation, together forming the single challenge described in candidate 0's prose.

The passage 'v'su lo midi' directly corresponds to the prose in 'Hishtachavah Source' which explicitly mentions 'v'su lo midi — and nothing more need be said' in the context of concluding that me'achas mehena cannot apply to avodah zarah.

The passage introduces Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda's report of the baraita comparing Shabbat stringencies to other mitzvot stringencies, which is exactly what the 'Shabbos Stricter' prose describes — the comparative baraita with chomer b'Shabbos and chomer b'sh'ar mitzvos, including the two melachos in one he'elam point.

All five items form one continuous examination of the baraita — the initial problem (items 1-2), Rabbi Yoḥanan's dismissal (item 3), the proposed avodah zarah resolution (item 4), and its rejection via the latter clause (item 5) — which is precisely what the 'Rejection Reason' prose describes in full.

The passage directly presents the Gemara's elimination of possible mis'asek scenarios in avodah zarah, which is precisely what the 'Mistaken Action' prose describes — the bowing-toward-synagogue case, the statue case, and the conclusion that there is no middle case parallel to mis'asek on Shabbos.

All three items trace the gemara's final attempts to resolve the braisa through meahava umiyirah and omer mutar, ending with the demonstration that neither works — exactly the 'unresolved' conclusion described in candidate 1's prose.
